what: Full pipeline closed with an OPEN-WEIGHT judge (no external API key, no egress) — GT PACE ICE
gpus: 2x A100-80GB (gen on GPU0, judge server on GPU1)

judge.serving: local vLLM OpenAI-compatible server (python -m vllm.entrypoints.openai.api_server --served-model-name judge), ready in ~135 s
judge.wiring: repo's OpenAiJudge pointed at it via OPENAI_BASE_URL=http://127.0.0.1:8000/v1 + OPENAI_API_KEY=sk-local-dummy + JUDGE_PROVIDER=openai
judge.code_change: ONE small env-gated patch in source/judge.py (JUDGE_NUMERIC_TEXT=1): open models tokenize numbers per-digit, so the single-token logprob trick collapses 0-100->0-9; the patch generates a few tokens and parses the integer instead. OpenAI logprob path unchanged by default.

stages_now_unblocked.vector_file: DONE — vector_source=open-judge-built (NOT the committed GPT-judged one); 10 effective pos/neg pairs passed threshold=50 filtering out of 1000 each

judge_score_sanity.note: pos-persona scored MORE humorous than neg-persona (23.9 > 18.4) and scores are graded 0-100 (std ~15-17), confirming the numeric-text judge works and is not degenerate

interpretation: Small positive Δτ (+1.2). Honest for THIS configuration: very early checkpoint (5k steps, near the emergence boundary), only 10 effective samples in the vector, coef 0.3, and a 7B judge noisier than the paper's GPT-4.1-mini. This VALIDATES the machinery (judge->filter->vector->steer->Δτ all run, key-free) — it is NOT a faithful reproduction of the paper's magnitudes.
caveats: Methodological substitution: Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct != paper's gpt-4.1-mini; numeric-text scoring != logprob aggregation. Do not compare Δτ to the paper.
Early checkpoint + n=5 eval / 10-sample vector => high variance.
For fidelity: use gpt-4.1-mini (or validate the open judge against it), a later checkpoint or larger n, and the logprob path.
cost_implication: On ICE the judge runs on a 2nd FREE GPU, so the judge-API cost (~$40 modeled for RQ1 with gpt-4.1-mini) -> ~$0 out-of-pocket. Full RQ1 grid on ICE is feasible at ~$0 cash (free instructional GPUs), bounded only by wall-clock + the 16-GPU-h/job cap.
